name: Measuring UX & Behavioral Impact
description: Rigorous methods for evaluating whether UX and behavioral design interventions are achieving their intended outcomes. Covers quantitative experimentation (A/B testing, multivariate testing), interpreting test results correctly (statistical significance, practical significance, confidence intervals), and integrating findings back into the design cycle. UX designers who measure impact close the design-behavior feedback loop.

subskills.name: A/B Testing
subskills.description: Controlled experiments comparing two variants (A=control, B=treatment) on a randomly split user population. Covers experiment design (hypothesis formulation, primary and guardrail metrics, minimum detectable effect), traffic splitting, sample size calculation, and avoiding common pitfalls (peeking, novelty effect, multiple testing problem).

subskills.name: Multivariate Testing (MVT)
subskills.description: Experiments testing multiple variables simultaneously to understand interaction effects between design elements. Covers full factorial vs fractional factorial designs, Taguchi methods, and interpreting interaction effects. Distinguishes MVT from sequential A/B tests and explains when each approach is appropriate (traffic volume requirements, timeline, hypothesis complexity).

subskills.name: Statistical Interpretation & Result Analysis
subskills.description: Correctly interpreting experiment results without common misinterpretations. Covers statistical significance vs practical significance, Type I errors (false positive), Type II errors (false negative), power analysis, effect size (Cohen's d), Bayesian vs frequentist approaches to testing, and confidence intervals vs p-values. Includes how to present results to non-technical stakeholders.

subskills.name: Integrating Test Results into Design
subskills.description: The process of translating experiment outcomes into actionable design decisions. Covers shipping winners, rolling back losers, analyzing segment-level heterogeneous treatment effects (HTE), deciding what to learn from failed experiments, documenting institutional knowledge, and building an experimentation culture that values learning over success rates.

subskills.name: UX & Behavioral Metrics Framework
subskills.description: Defining and tracking the right metrics for behavioral design outcomes. Covers HEART framework (Happiness, Engagement, Adoption, Retention, Task Success), North Star Metric, leading vs lagging indicators, behavioral funnels (activation → engagement → retention → revenue), and custom behavioral metrics that measure the specific target action.

junior.description: Understands A/B test mechanics and can define primary behavioral metrics using the HEART framework.

mid.description: Interprets experiment results correctly (avoiding p-value misinterpretation), translates outcomes into design decisions, and documents learnings systematically.

senior.description: Designs and analyzes multivariate experiments with interaction effects, leads experimentation culture, and integrates behavioral metrics into organizational OKR frameworks.
